findings.obligation: A rule the code checks at runtime, or only in a test, that the types could make impossible is a finding (nw-type-level-design, 'Decide before writing' 4 and 'Write' 3; nw-certainty-by-construction).
findings.observation: Open and unchanged by the delta; retained as non-blocking. Resume still models a four-way partition of the plan's positions as four parallel public collections, to_read, carried, already_read and skipped, the fourth added by this feature. Nothing in the type stops one position appearing in two of them; the disjointness the count depends on is asserted only by property tests. Resume::kept at resume.rs:104-125 already rebuilds the per-position-with-disposition sequence the type could carry, and the revised oracle binding now consumes exactly that sequence (sut_picked_up reads verdict.kept()), so the shape the type is missing is the one the oracle already reads. The owner states that reshaping Resume would disturb that binding; the remediation below keeps kept(), to_read, carried, already_read and skipped as public observations, so the binding and tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_and_accounts_core.rs:402 are unaffected.
findings.remediation: Carry the verdict as one sequence of positions each with its disposition - the KeptRow shape already introduced, extended with the carried-skip reason - and derive to_read, carried, already_read, skipped and kept() over it, so no two of them can name the same position and every current reader keeps its surface. Not required for this feature; schedule it with the next change to the resume verdict.

Finding 1 is resolved at the right owner, and resolved in the oracle. tests/acceptance/review_app_repos_read_across_resume.rs now reads the surface it previously refused: sut_picked_up returns verdict.kept() as KeptRepo { position, carries_an_earlier_read: row.status == PlanRowStatus::Read }, so Resume::already_read and Resume::kept reach the assertions through production's own answer instead of a literal. The new broad property a_run_picking_a_paused_scan_up_keeps_every_repo_the_scan_already_read asserts set equality in both directions, kept_as_read == already_read(&paused.plan), so neither a dropped read nor an invented one passes; its expected value is computed from the generated plan's own RowState::AlreadyRead rows and never from production, so it is not circular. Its generator a_paused_scan_with_reads_to_keep is a prop_oneof of three, every branch built on a_paused_scan_read_part_way, so every case holds at least one already-read row and at least one still-to-read row; the third branch, a_paused_scan_read_by_a_source_she_has_since_removed, forces exactly the case nothing observed before: an already-read row whose account fails its check now AND whose source the owner has removed. acceptance.md records the new row against P1 and P2 with that locator, and corrects the stale caveat on the twice-picked-up journey. L3 now takes its positions from the kept plan rather than from reads_now, which widens the within-the-plan, plan-order and each-position-once assertion to the carried and already-read shares; kept is a superset of reads_now, so no discrimination is lost. The oracle reviewer's own record (docs/feature/fix-repos-read-across-resume/runs/review.oracle.S1.json, observations R16-R18, findings empty) cites the semantic RED it observed on the regression this property names.

Finding 4 is resolved. crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs now carries a RunPosition(usize) newtype documented as a row's position in THIS run's own frozen plan, the only position mark_repo_read may be given; read_planned takes &[(RunPosition, PlanSource, PlannedRepo)] and unwraps it only at the store call (position.0), and both producers, scan_accounts and ResumedPlan, build it explicitly. The two position spaces can no longer be interchanged in the direction that reaches the store. The stale bindings are renamed for what they are: kept_row for a KeptRow, picked_up_position for a position of the plan being picked up, position_in_this_run for the index into the resuming run's own rows, with a comment at the point where the two spaces part. Behaviour is unchanged: the same values flow to the same calls.
